source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #350 (branch fix/330-char-validation at head 3f20c2e074dff12d5eb393ef75b2e40779d11ab6 — the #330 change (core-to-component char conversions trap with the canonical ‘invalid `char` bit pattern’ message, funnelled through the shared char_from_canonical_bits helper in the flat lift and memory read paths) merged with current main 21edef0f0b147af7a43dcbec002673227ff8516d (PRs #348 and #351), with no merge conflicts; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45581296266, 45581315051 and 45581332674 against the branch and pull-request run 45581280272, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #350 (#330, core-to-component char conversions trap with the canonical ‘invalid `char` bit pattern’ message). The branch merged current main (merge commit 3f20c2e, main at 21edef0f0b147af7a43dcbec002673227ff8516d — PR #348 (#342, canonical lift/lower transfers resource handles across component call boundaries) and PR #351 (#331, trap invalid variant discriminants with the canonical message) on top of the main at 90f1437b1445b8523daa2f78eecb366de415ed11 the branch had merged during integration); the merge was conflict-free, and its CI run on the merged tree tripped the gate on six series, all in the release-size profile. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45581400712, 45581419487 and 45581439929 on main at 21edef0f0b147af7a43dcbec002673227ff8516d; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline). Against the checked-in baseline, the main control is byte-identical on 25 of the 32 gated series; on seven series it measures below that baseline — stripped file and stripped .text −32 B in release for component, stripped file −48 B and stripped .text −32 B in release for wasi and wasi-threads, and stripped file −16 B in release-size for wasi-threads — because that baseline was snapshotted from PR #348's branch tree and the squash-merged main measures slightly smaller (the gate passes shrinkage, so the staleness was inert). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped .text +32 B in each of component, wasi and wasi-threads and stripped file +16 B in each of wasi and wasi-threads (component stripped file is unchanged); in release-size, stripped file +128 B (component), +128 B (wasi) and +144 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +80 B, +80 B and +96 B. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. In release the growth is absorbed by the staleness headroom, so only the six release-size series exceed the checked-in baseline; those six are re-baselined to the branch measurements. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is unchanged: the release component stripped file series at +10.29% (2,433,656 B to 2,683,928 B), whose baseline does not move in this re-baseline; the release core-nosimd stripped file series is likewise unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
